extracted.intended_audience: EPA officials, environmental justice advocates, regulated recipients and their counsel, and civil rights lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluation criteria used by EPA (and stakeholders) to assess Title VI administrative complaints challenging environmental permits and to guide recipients' compliance/permitting practices under Draft/Interim Title VI Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse disparate impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Draft Revised Investigation Guidance provides an analytical framework for determining adverse disparate impacts (the proposed adverse disparate impact analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance provides a detailed discussion of the proposed adverse disparate impact analysis (65 Fed. Reg. at 39,677–82). The agency anticipated that parts of the adverse disparate impact analysis would be altered or omitted based on the facts and totality of the circumstances in each complaint (id.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider in area-specific agreements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Area-specific agreements may establish pollutant ceilings with steady reductions over time; the period over which reductions should occur will vary with a number of factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include the magnitude of the adverse disparate impact, the number and types of sources involved, the scale of the geographic area, the pathways of exposure, and the number of people in the affected population. Area-specific agreements need not be limited to one environmental media and may cover several media (e.g., air and water). Pre-existing obligations under environmental laws might not be sufficient to constitute an agreement meriting due weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential approach to disproportionate impact analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: SAB recommended performing disproportionate impact analyses in a sequential manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations included determining potential risk to all populations before estimating disproportionate impact, developing the Cumulative Outdoor Air Toxics Concentration Exposure Methodology further, evaluating cancer risks and non-cancer health effects separately when analyzing potential risks of emitted chemicals, and maintaining good communications with local residents by conveying health-impact study information (EPA SAB IHEC report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient definition
rubrics_metrics.description: [R]ecipient means for the purposes of this regulation, any state or its political subdivision, any instrumentality of a state or its political subdivision, any public or private agency, institution, organization, or other entity, or any person to which Federal financial assistance is extended directly or through another recipient, including any successor, assignee, or transferee of a recipient, but excluding the ultimate beneficiary of the assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted directly from Draft Questions and Answers; used to determine who is covered by the Draft Recipient Guidance and Draft Revised Investigation Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft guidance does not create enforceable rights/obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Draft Recipient Guidance and the Draft Revised Investigation Guidance serve solely as guidance and do not create enforceable rights or obligations enforceable by any party in litigation with the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 65 Fed. Reg. at 39,656; the Drafts are intended to provide a framework rather than binding legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient burden to demonstrate significant emission decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: If a permit action will significantly decrease overall emissions or pollutants of concern at the facility named in the complaint, EPA usually would not initiate an investigation of allegations regarding cumulative impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient has the burden of demonstrating that the decrease at a particular facility is actual and significant. The decreases should be in the same media and from the same facility that is alleged in the complaint (Mank, citing Draft Guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA will assess whether impacts result from factors within recipient's authority
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a recipient is in violation of Title VI or EPA's implementing regulations, the Agency expects to assess whether the adverse disparate impact results from factors within the recipient's authority to consider as defined by applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 65 Fed. Reg. language emphasized by the Report; the 'within authority' inquiry is a threshold/merits consideration in investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of adverse impact analysis: spectrum vs focused studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse impact analyses may focus on a spectrum of potential adverse impacts (as in the Draft Revised Investigation Guidance) or may be more focused, such as the impact of a specific pollutant on nearby populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: a study regarding the impact of lead emissions on blood lead levels in the surrounding area. EPA may use either broad cumulative analyses or pollutant-specific analyses depending on complaint facts (65 Fed. Reg. at 39,653).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of cumulative impacts and when EPA will not investigate
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA usually would not initiate an investigation of allegations regarding cumulative impacts if a permit action will significantly decrease pollutants at the facility complained about, provided the recipient proves the decrease is real and significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differentiation between decreases at a facility and in a specific area is used to determine whether cumulative-impact inquiries are necessary (Mank, Too Much Discretion for EPA, p. 11164).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of cancer vs non-cancer health effects separately
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyzing potential risks of emitted chemicals for the purposes of determining whether cumulative risks are minimal, EPA (via SAB recommendations) advised evaluating cancer risks and non-cancer health effects separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of SAB's recommendations to improve disproportionate impact methodologies (EPA-SAB-IHEC-99-007).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain communications with affected communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain good communications with residents of local communities by conveying information about health impact studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAB recommendation; part of best practices for investigations and analyses to ensure transparency and community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) and informal resolution participation
rubrics_metrics.description: ADR includes a variety of approaches including the use of a third party neutral acting as a mediator or the use of a structured process through which the parties can participate in shared learning and creative problem solving to reach a consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft Guidance references ADR; Shintech recommended EPA involve complainants in informal resolution to avoid delay and litigation. NEJAC and others noted disadvantages and cautioned about ADR; stakeholders differ on ADR's appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines and exhaustion of administrative remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a grievance with the recipient does not satisfy the requirement that complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged discriminatory acts; the Draft Guidance was criticized for forcing complainants to file before exhausting administrative remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40 C.F.R. § 7.120(b)(2) and related comments: complainants must file Title VI complaints within 180 days; the guidance's interaction with exhaustion requirements and administrative processes was a point of contention (NEJAC comments, Cole comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR notification timeframe for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 calendar days from the start of the compliance review or complaint investigation, the OCR will notify the recipient in writing by certified mail of preliminary findings, recommendations for voluntary compliance (if any), and the recipient's right to engage in voluntary compliance negotiations where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40 C.F.R. § 7.115 sets this timeline and required content for notification (preliminary findings; recommendations; right to voluntary compliance negotiations).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA will consider all pertinent information including recipient submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considers all pertinent information related to an investigation, including information submitted by recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted in Higginbotham letter and Draft Guidance Q&A; indicates investigations are fact-sensitive and recipients have opportunity to submit materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for single definitions of key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders noted the Draft Guidance does not provide single definitions to important terms such as 'adverse disparate impact,' 'adequate justification,' 'comparison populations,' or 'affected populations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry and local government commenters argued lack of clear definitions creates uncertainty and gives EPA broad discretion (Lyons letter; Dennis W. Archer; comment summaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance applicability exclusions and future guidance topics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA reminded recipients that the Title VI guidance did not apply to other issues, such as enforcement-related matters and adequacy of public participation; these topics would be addressed in future EPA guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 65 Fed. Reg. at 39,670; Draft Guidance thus limited immediate applicability to certain permit-related Title VI issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional review pursuant to 40 C.F.R. Part 7
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducts jurisdictional reviews of Title VI complaints pursuant to 40 C.F.R. Part 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gail Ginsberg testimony: jurisdictional review is conducted pursuant to EPA's Title VI regulations found at 40 C.F.R. Part 7; jurisdictional (threshold) issues affect whether the Office of Civil Rights will proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for federally recognized Indian tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Draft Revised Investigation Guidance does not address complaints against EPA recipients that are federally recognized Indian tribes; EPA intends to provide different guidance taking into account federal Indian law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA plans continued collaboration with tribes and DOJ to develop tailored guidance (Draft Q&A, p.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critiques of timeframes and open-endedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders (NPRA, Chevron, Environmental Council of the States) described EPA's timeframes as unnecessarily lengthy and open-ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments reflect that protracted or vague timelines undermine predictability for recipients and complainants; part of public comment evaluation of Draft Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of census and industry-emissions data to analyze disproportionate burden
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA and others have used census data (e.g., 1990 census) and estimates of industry-reported emissions to analyze whether a disproportionate burden exists on particular communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University of Michigan case study (Shintech) example: EPA analyzed disproportionate burden using census and emissions estimates; demonstrates types of data used in analyses.
